title: 시장에서 깎기: 조금만 깎아 주세요
objective: Ask the price, say it is expensive, and ask for a discount with "-(으)세요".
summary: A fruit-stall conversation: ask the price and politely ask for a discount.
setting: A fruit stall at a traditional Korean market. A customer wants apples and tries to get a better price.

task.title: Ask, judge, and bargain
task.line: Use the dialogue and the word list to choose, fill in, order, or say the right Korean.

words.meaning: please give me a discount (lit. please cut the price)
words.exampleMeaning: I'm buying two. Please give me a discount.

words.meaning: a polite way to call a shop owner or seller
bag (a counter for things sold in plastic bags)

words.exampleMeaning: Just a few chili peppers, please.

dialogue.meaning: Excuse me (sir/ma'am), how much are these apples?
That's a bit expensive. Please give me a small discount.

dialogue.korean: 한 봉지는 안 돼요. 두 봉지에 만 팔천 원 해 드릴게요.
dialogue.meaning: Not for one bag. I'll give you two bags for 18,000 won.

dialogue.korean: 좋아요. 두 봉지 주세요. 여기 만 팔천 원이요.
dialogue.meaning: Okay. Two bags, please. Here's 18,000 won.
Haha, thank you. Please come again.

exercises: Choose the right word: 사장님, 이 모자 ( 얼마예요 / 깎아 주세요 )?
Change the verb in brackets to the -(으)세요 form: ① 내일 또 ____. (오다) ② 여기 ____. (앉다) ③ 천천히 ____. (보다)
Put the words in order to make one sentence: 주세요 / 두 개 / 만 원에
Read and answer in Korean: 사장님: 귤 한 봉지에 오천 원이에요. 손님: 두 봉지 구천 원에 주세요. 사장님: 네, 좋아요. — How much does the customer pay?
What do you say? The seller says, "한 개에 삼천 원이에요." You think it is too expensive. Say it is expensive and ask for a discount.
answers: ① 오세요 ② 앉으세요 ③ 보세요
두 개 만 원에 주세요. (만 원에 두 개 주세요.)
좀 비싸요. 깎아 주세요. (너무 비싸요. 조금만 깎아 주세요.)
